subject: Re: Sentryly demo — hosted onramp, endpoints & rate limits
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Alex Thompson <alex@sentrly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentryly demo — hosted onramp, endpoints & rate limits

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time to walk through the demo today. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can size a Hosted evaluation that mirrors your production footprint.

Recap (from our side)
- Primary use case: customer support summarization + routing (inbound chat + email).
- Expected traffic shape: bursty during business hours, peak windows around 11am–1pm PST and 3pm–4pm PST.
- Data sensitivity: a small fraction of PII (~3% of messages contain masked SSNs or DOBs) — you said this is acceptable to store with controls, but procurement may push for VPC if needed.

What we need to qualify Hosted as the immediate onramp
1) Traffic profile: estimated QPS at peak and typical RPS outside peaks; avg tokens in prompt + completion (a sample will do).
2) Endpoint mapping: will you want a single multi-purpose completion endpoint, or separate endpoints for short replies vs long-form summarization? This affects batching and token economics.
3) Rate tolerance: what's the max acceptable per-request latency for interactive flows (SLO target)? Are 200–400ms p50 comfortable, or is <150ms required for core flows?
4) Security/compliance: if procurement insists on Private/VPC, can you share the procurement contact so we can start the Private checklist in parallel?

Proposed short plan
- We can provision a sandbox Hosted endpoint (read-only logs, token billing enabled) for a 2-week pilot. Suggested initial rate cap: 75 concurrent token streams / 500 rps with burst to 800 rps for short spikes — we can tighten/relax after you share traffic numbers.
- Attach: mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed milestones, responsibilities).

Next steps
- Alex: send a rough CSV with hourly QPS and avg token sizes, and confirm whether you prefer one or two endpoints for the pilot.
- Priyom/Ben: we’ll provision sandbox and share endpoint + API key and a short checklist for prefix/KV caching to reduce token costs.

If you want, we can also schedule an ops deep-dive this week with Monica to walk network egress, logging, and SSO.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
pri_yom@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment(s): mutual-action-plan.xlsx

From: Alex Thompson <alex@sentrly.ai>

Cc: Sentryly Procurement <procurement@sentrly.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sentryly demo — hosted onramp, endpoints & rate limits

Priyom — great recap, thanks. Quick answers inline.

Traffic & tokens
- Typical weekdays: 120–150 rps; peaks up to 700 rps on heavy incident days (maybe 1–3 hours/week). Weekend baseline ~40 rps.
- Avg prompt tokens: 120 tokens. Avg completion: 90 tokens for summarization; ~350 tokens for long-form suggested responses (rare).

Endpoints
- Prefer two endpoints for the pilot: 
  1) short-reply (summaries & quick suggestions)
  2) long-response (drafted replies / suggested articles)

Latency SLO
- For short-reply flows we target p95 < 450ms; for long-response p95 < 1.2s is OK. Anything above that will impact UX.

Security / procurement
- Procurement is watching for any data residency / access-control language. If Private/VPC is required, our procurement lead (procurement@sentrly.ai) will raise the checklist. For now procurement is open to Hosted with SOC2 evidence.

Attachments
- I attached an anonymized hourly export we use for capacity planning (see "sentryly_hourly_sample.csv" - attached to this reply).

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Thompson
Head of Product | Sentryly
alex@sentrly.ai

Attachment(s): sentryly_hourly_sample.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentryly demo — hosted onramp, endpoints & rate limits

Priyom — quick internal note based on Alex's numbers.

A few operational pointers:
- Two endpoints is the right move: it lets us tune batching/queue depth separately (short-reply can be aggressive batching with small max tokens; long-response we cap concurrency).
- Suggested trial caps: start short-reply at 1,000 rps with a per-client concurrency limit (to avoid a single key consuming capacity), long-response at 200 rps. We'll monitor usage and auto-hike if pattern is stable.
- KV/prefix caching: recommend they ship a 7-day hotcache window for conversation context — biggest wins in token reduction.
- Compliance: attach trimmed SOC2-extract.pdf (sanitized) we can push to procurement. If procurement insists on VPC, start the Private scoping now; lead time ~6 weeks.

I'll sponsor provisioning once Priyom confirms the HubSpot deal stage and we have the sample CSV.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alex — thanks for the sample and the clarity, this is exactly what we need. Next steps from here: 

1) We’ll provision two sandbox endpoints today (short-reply, long-response) and share keys + rate caps. Initial configuration:
   - short-reply: 500 rps, burst to 1,000; per-key concurrency limit 50
   - long-response: 150 rps; per-key concurrency limit 20
2) Ben will share the SOC2 extract (attached) and a brief ops checklist for SSO/network egress before EOD.
3) Procurement: thanks for looping in procurement@sentrly.ai — Ben/Monica can coordinate on the Private scoping if you need it.
4) We’ll stand up a 14-day pilot with monitoring dashboards (latency, token usage, error rates). At day 7 we’ll review thresholds and consider increasing caps.

Please confirm that the above config looks safe to start. If so, we’ll send API keys and a one-page onboarding note with code snippets for prefix caching.

Looking forward — Priyom
